text:
My partner and I are planning to get married in October and then begin the process of bringing her to Israel as my spouse.

About a month ago, we applied for a tourist visa so she could visit Israel before the wedding. Today, we received a refusal because we had not provided enough evidence of our ongoing communication. We have a huge amount of correspondence, but I only attached a few examples because I thought that would be sufficient.

They also said she had not demonstrated sufficient ties outside Israel. She lives and works legally in a third country, but apparently we did not provide enough proof of her employment and legal status there. Although we submitted everything listed in the requirements, it seems they also expected her work visa or residence permit.

We are now gathering the additional documents and preparing an internal appeal.

Could this tourist visa refusal affect her future application to move to Israel as my spouse? 

Is it still worth appealing if the original travel dates are no longer relevant?
